review.summary:
changes_needed
A crash between remote task creation and checkpointing still duplicates work.
The A2A API table mixes incompatible version details.
Default blocking SendMessage can bypass the advertised deadline.
Checks: 27 tests passed; link checker reported bad 0.

findings.checklist_item: A. Accuracy: code sketches must match resumability claims
findings.title: Qualify recovery across the remote-send/checkpoint gap
findings.claim: The saved-task lookup fixes restarting during polling, but a crash after the remote task is created and before store.save succeeds still creates a second task on restart. The subsequent claim that checkpointing prevents duplicate tasks after a crash is therefore too broad.
findings.evidence: Executed the extracted sketch with a fake remote server and a store that crashes before its first durable save. The server retained task 1 while the checkpoint contained an empty remote mapping. Restarting from that checkpoint created task 2. This is the same sent-but-not-recorded failure explained in 3.5.
findings.proposed_change: Add a dated caveat distinguishing recovery after the task-id checkpoint from an ambiguous send before that checkpoint. To guarantee one task across both cases, describe an explicit server-supported deduplication or reconciliation contract using a stable request identity. Test crashes immediately before and after the task-id save.

findings.checklist_item: A. Accuracy: API names, versions and behavior
findings.title: Align the A2A API details and sketch with version 1.0
findings.claim: The table declares v1.0.0 but gives incompatible message-role and task-state identifiers. The sketch also uses DataPart, which the v1 migration replaces with a unified Part. Without a documented normalization adapter, the state comparisons do not match v1 responses.
findings.evidence: The official [v1 migration guide](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/whats-new-v1/) specifies ROLE_USER/ROLE_AGENT, TASK_STATE_* enum values, and replacement of separate DataPart/TextPart/FilePart types by Part. The [v1.0.0 specification](https://a2a-protocol.org/v1.0.0/specification/) shows state under task.status.state. The notes instead list user/agent and compare task.state with INPUT_REQUIRED and COMPLETED.
findings.proposed_change: Use the v1 identifiers and object shapes in the API table. Either update the sketch accordingly or explicitly define its adapter as normalizing protocol objects into the abbreviated teaching representation. Verify a completed response and both interrupted states using v1-shaped fixtures.

findings.checklist_item: A. Accuracy: defaults and deadline enforcement
findings.title: Request nonblocking task creation before entering the polling loop
findings.claim: The sketch assumes send_message returns an active task immediately. A2A's default send behavior waits for a terminal or interrupted state, so the initial call can consume the entire remote execution before the task id is saved or the deadline is checked.
findings.evidence: The [v1.0.0 specification, SendMessageConfiguration](https://a2a-protocol.org/v1.0.0/specification/) defines returnImmediately as false by default and requires that mode to wait for completion or interruption. For exercise (b), an uninterrupted 12-minute task can therefore finish before the sketch reaches its 10-minute deadline check.
findings.proposed_change: Explicitly request returnImmediately=true through the chosen adapter and bound the initial network call by the remaining deadline. State that the adapter returns a task for this example. Check that the 12-minute fake task returns its handle immediately and is canceled at the 10-minute cap.

findings.checklist_item: A. Accuracy: protocol capabilities and contradictions between lessons
findings.title: Distinguish A2A from MCP without implying MCP is synchronous only
findings.claim: The motivation implies that wrapping a remote agent as an MCP tool cannot support ongoing work or requests for input. That conflicts with 9.2's explanation of input-required results and the Tasks extension. Those capabilities are not exclusive reasons to choose A2A.
findings.evidence: The official [MCP Tasks extension](https://tasks.extensions.modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/tasks) allows tools/call to return an asynchronous task handle, exposes working/input_required/completed states, and supports additional input through tasks/update. Section 9.2 already mentions both input-required results and the Tasks extension.
findings.proposed_change: Qualify the limitation as applying to a simple synchronous wrapper. Explain that MCP also supports asynchronous tasks and input requests, while A2A supplies the agent-facing contracts discussed here, such as Agent Cards, messages and artifacts. Preserve the email wording with a corrective note if necessary.

findings.checklist_item: A. Accuracy: arithmetic and worked answers
findings.title: Count the seed consistently in the blackboard infection rate
findings.claim: The stated infection range does not follow from the number of copying workers and the lesson's lineage-based definition. The seed itself counts as infected, as answer A explicitly demonstrates.
findings.evidence: There are five W2 verdicts. With two to four copying workers plus the original seed, three to five verdicts reach the seed: 60–100%, rather than 50–80%. Computing these cases gives copy rates of 40%, 60%, 80% and infection rates of 60%, 80%, 100%.
findings.proposed_change: Add a correction stating 60–100% of W2 verdicts under these assumptions, or provide explicit counts and a different denominator supporting the reported range. Keep the denominator consistent when comparing topologies.
